conviction_note: Two opposing company-level facts. The US line grew only about 2.5% q/q in Q2 ($91.6M vs ~$89M implied in Q1), and consensus needs roughly 4-8% q/q in Q3. Against that, German pricing talks were guided to conclude in Q3 against a reserve the company called conservative, so a true-up could fill the gap. Misses on this name have been sold for 8-14 points and beats bought for about 4, with downside skew of +4.06 and a +5.2% 5-day run-up. So p_up sits at 47 on a 9-point absolute move (implied 8.23%, under-sizing corrected upward). impact_sum (-0.8) and the scaled number (-0.54) agree in sign and size.

positioning_check: Short interest 2,936,047 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 9.9% of shares outstanding (BlackRock's 13G/A implies ~29.5M shares). That is down 15.5% from 3,475,527 on 09-30. Days to cover 10.33 on 284k ADV (https://altindex.com/ticker/krys/short-interest, fetched 2026-10-30). Shorts were covering into the print. findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call (2026-08-03) that German Vyjuvek pricing negotiations were expected to conclude in Q3 2026. Q2 carried a full-quarter German pricing reserve, accrued 'conservatively', with the aim to 'true up once pricing is set'. That reserve left Europe+Japan revenue flat at $27.6M. If pricing was set in Q3 above the accrual, the Q3 print can carry a retroactive catch-up plus a higher German run-rate on a bar ($124.7-128.6M) that the 10-26 preview framed only as downside risk (delay or larger reserve).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same line hit Q2. Flat ex-US revenue from the German reserve drove a ~$3-4M revenue miss, and the stock fell 8.37% on 2026-08-03. No German true-up has ever printed, so there is no history of a positive surprise on this line. Beats on this name have bought about +4% (2026-01-12, 2026-02-17).
findings.why_not_priced: The only sourced Q3 preview (finviz, 2026-10-26) frames Germany solely as downside: 'a delay or a settlement that forces a larger reserve true-up' would push normalization to 2027. The company's own 'conservative accrual' wording implies the asymmetric case is upward. If the market expected an upside true-up, the consensus would sit above the ~5% q/q step from $119.2M and the skew would not be +4 vol points downside. The G-BA benefit resolution was dated 2026-02-19, and the AMNOG negotiation clock runs about 6 months from it, so a Q3 conclusion is plausible.
findings.independence: The G-BA resolution of 2026-02-19 (https://www.g-ba.de/downloads/39-1464-7698/2026-02-19_AM-RL-XII_Beremagen-geperpavec_D-1229_EN.pdf) independently dates the start of the statutory price-negotiation window. No source confirms a German price (Erstattungsbetrag) was actually agreed. The finviz preview (shared topic, different author) treats it as a risk.

findings.finding: US Vyjuvek revenue grew only about 2.5% q/q in Q2 2026: $91.6M against about $89M implied for Q1, where Q1 total was $116.4M and ex-US was described as 'broadly flat' at $27.6M. Management said new US patients skew 'moderate to mild', which use less product. The Q3 consensus of $124.7-128.6M implies +5-8% q/q total. Absent a German true-up, with ex-US about $28-30M and Italy/Spain not yet launched, the US would need $95-99M, or +4-8% q/q, roughly double Q2's pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses on this name have been sold hard: -14.06% (2025-05-06), -14.04% (2025-08-04), -8.37% (2026-08-03, a $3-4M revenue miss despite an EPS beat). The Q3 2025 print, roughly in line, moved +0.17%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews cite a 'not heroic' bar based on the four-quarter total trend, which mixes in ex-US launch growth. They do not split out the US q/q deceleration from the Q2 split. If the market had priced US deceleration, the consensus would have been cut toward ~$122M after the Q2 miss. Instead Benzinga shows $129.6M in September and $128.6M in October, and the stock ran +5% into the print. The +4 downside skew is the partial counter: some of this is priced.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001711279/000171127926000044/a1q26exhibit991pr.htm) gives the $116.4M total that the Q1 US figure is derived from. The 'milder new patients' wording is from the Q2 call transcript (https://longbridge.com/news/295468489). Both are primary company statements, but the Q3 extrapolation is inference. Net of the rest: finding 1's German true-up is the offsetting line, sized separately.

findings.finding: The stock ran from $311.50 (2026-10-26 close per the finviz/Trefis previews) to $327.83 (+5.24% over 5 days) into the print. Short interest fell 15.5% to 2.94M shares in the first half of October, so shorts covered into the event. Combined with call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.27), this lifts the bar on the reaction and removes some squeeze fuel for an upside surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-03 print came after a ~9% slide the month before and still fell 8.4%. No clear history of run-ups into prints on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: This is itself the market's positioning, so it is priced by construction. It is filed because it changes the reaction function: a crowded short that is being covered gives less upside convexity on a beat.
findings.independence: The $311.50 10-26 price is from finviz (https://finviz.com/news/407879/krystal-biotechs-germany-pricing-drag-tests-whether-vyjuvek-demand-can-carry-q3). The run-up and the P/C ratio come from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Several readouts are guided to 'before year end' or 4Q 2026 and could be bundled into the Nov 2 business update. These are: the KB803 IOLITE registrational topline (corneal abrasions in DEB, 16 patients, crossover, guided 4Q 2026), the KB407 CF 5-patient interim, the KB111 HALITE-1 ~7-patient interim, and the FDA alignment on the KB407 registrational design (4Q 2026). None had been released as of 2026-10-30; the only interim update since Q2 is the KB113 Gorlin data of 10-15.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KB407 interim (2026-01) and Gorlin data (2026-10-15) were released standalone, not with a print. No record of pipeline readouts bundled into an earnings release.
findings.why_not_priced: Timing is unknown; the company may release these standalone after the window. The sign is unknown. These raise the width of the outcome distribution, not its center, which is why the size is 0 and the band is wide.
findings.independence: The 10-26 finviz preview also lists IOLITE data as 'promised this year' and says the NK program (KB801) has drifted to early 2027 (https://finviz.com/news/407879/krystal-biotechs-germany-pricing-drag-tests-whether-vyjuvek-demand-can-carry-q3).

findings.finding: Japan listed Vyjuvek on the NHI price list and launched it on 2025-10-22. Under Japan's new-drug rule, the 14-day prescription limit (a renewal burden management flagged on the Q2 call) lapses after the first listing year, i.e. from November 2026. That lets the Q3 call frame Q4 Japan refill compliance constructively.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history of a Japan-specific surprise. Japan sits inside the Europe+Japan line ($27.6M in Q2).
findings.source_date: 2025-10 (listing approved at the Chuikyo 2025-10-15 meeting, listed 2025-10-22)
findings.why_not_priced: Japanese-language trade-press fact. US previews mention the Japan renewal burden only as a risk, without the date it ends. This is inference from the listing rule, not a company statement, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The listing date is also on nk.jiho.jp (https://nk.jiho.jp/article/202661). The Q2 call mentions the Japan renewal burden (https://longbridge.com/news/295468489).

outside_window.finding: Italy and Spain commercial launches are guided 'before year end 2026'. France pricing runs into 2027, and the UK (MHRA approval May 2026) is in pricing talks. These are revenue contributions after the window; only commentary lands on Nov 2.

baseline_tension: The US-deceleration negative agrees with the +4.06 downside skew, so it is partly priced. The German true-up positive cuts against both the skew and the only preview's framing. The +5.2% run-up with shorts covering cuts against an upside squeeze. Net is close to balanced with a slight downside lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 and lesson 1: the German true-up is partly a retroactive one-off in revenue, and this name pays about +4% for beats. The German finding went from +1.5 to +1.0.
Lesson 7: about 10 days to cover and roughly 10% of shares short shrink the US-deceleration negative from -2.0 to -1.6. The skew agrees with that finding, so it is also partly priced.
Lesson 6: the revenue bar comes from three sources within 3% of each other, so it is usable. The EPS bar is disputed and is not used.
Lesson 9: the US-segment finding is sized net of the ex-US offset, which is filed separately as the German true-up finding. Findings 3, 4 and 5 are unchanged.
